subject.title: [Feature]: Opt-in hook to log group messages blocked by channel access policy

question: Should OpenClaw expose blocked inbound group messages to plugins as a supported cross-channel Plugin SDK lifecycle event, and if so should the first release be generic or explicitly WhatsApp-only?
rationale: The proposal adds a new public plugin capability and a configuration surface at an authorization boundary; source-level implementation alone cannot determine the intended long-term API scope, payload privacy contract, or channel-consistency promise.

options.title: Design a generic inbound decision hook
options.body: Define one documented event with normalized allow/block reason and privacy rules, then add channel implementations as they meet that contract.

options.title: Approve a narrowly scoped WhatsApp experiment
options.body: Ship an explicitly WhatsApp-only, opt-in observation contract with documentation that it is not yet a cross-channel SDK guarantee.

options.title: Keep blocked messages private
options.body: Decline the hook and direct archival use cases to channel-native exports or a separately approved audit design.

recommendation.title: Design a generic inbound decision hook
recommendation.body: Define one documented event with normalized allow/block reason and privacy rules, then add channel implementations as they meet that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the concrete proposed integration and companion-plugin use case, but broader Plugin SDK ownership should be assigned by maintainers after the API direction is chosen.
